# Herdr Obsidian Vault

> Two Herdr desktop-app mods: a side panel that browses and searches an Obsidian vault, and a floating reader that draws notes (callouts, wikilinks, embeds, images, PDFs, math, Mermaid, Excalidraw, Canvas). Read-only, no bundled binaries. macOS is the only OS the author uses; Linux and Windows code paths are implemented and covered by fake-platform unit tests but not run in the live app.

Facts an agent needs:

- Install both folders, mods/vault and mods/vault-reader, into the mods folder of the Herdr home, under exactly these names. Never overwrite a mod of the same name. Merge keys.json. Run herdr-app check on both mods. The mods have place "none": the key in keys.json (ctrl-shift-m, mod.open:vault) opens the panel as a popup in any layout, Herdr's own main included; to dock it, add a block {"mod": "vault"} to a layout of the person's own.
- Mods are JavaScript for gpui-kit (native GPUI, no DOM, no Node APIs). Herdr reloads a mod when any file in its folder changes: never write there at run time. Caches go to data/vault in the Herdr home.
- Requirements: only Herdr. Optional: ripgrep (search), Node.js 22.4+ and a Chromium-family browser and the Obsidian app (math, Mermaid, Excalidraw), Poppler (all PDF pages), curl (web images). A missing program is named in the UI, never a crash. A browser or Obsidian in an unusual place: keys browser and asar (absolute paths) in data/vault/settings.json. Vaults must be inside the home folder.
- Tell the person before installing: the mods read the vault folder and Obsidian's vault list, run rg, node, a headless browser, pdftoppm, pdfinfo, curl and the system opener, download web images shown by notes (switch: the Web images button, or remoteImages in data/vault/settings.json), and write only under data/vault.
- Stable contract: mod names vault and vault-reader; shared keys vault.list, vault.current, vault.open (and vault.outside, added beside them); commands vault.add, vault.import; tab name obsidian. The mod folder name is spelled once per mod, in mod-name.js.
- Tests: npm test (Node 22.4+, no dependencies; not `node --test tests/`), node scripts/check-repo.mjs, node scripts/check-recipe.mjs, node scripts/install-sim.mjs, node scripts/privacy-scan.mjs, node scripts/check-docs.mjs, herdr-app check on each mod folder. Do not drive a live Herdr window.
- Not verified: Linux and Windows have not been seen running in the live Herdr app, and the CI workflow (scripts/ci.workflow.yml) is a template that has not run. Say so; never write that it works there. Herdr's runtime has no TextDecoder, TextEncoder, structuredClone or Intl, and localeCompare ignores its options.
- No personal data in files or commits. Not affiliated with Obsidian; the Obsidian logo is not distributed.

- [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/<owner>/herdr-obsidian-vault/blob/main/AGENTS.md): install, adapt, test and edit safely
- [README](https://github.com/<owner>/herdr-obsidian-vault/blob/main/README.md): what it is, install, requirements, privacy
- [RECIPE.md](https://github.com/<owner>/herdr-obsidian-vault/blob/main/RECIPE.md): the brief to rebuild the mods
- [Install](https://<owner>.github.io/herdr-obsidian-vault/install.html): the one-line installer, agent prompt, manual copy, options
- [Usage](https://<owner>.github.io/herdr-obsidian-vault/usage.html): showing the panel, search, reader, keys, what is drawn
- [Requirements](https://<owner>.github.io/herdr-obsidian-vault/requirements.html): per-OS table and what happens without each program
- [Configuration](https://<owner>.github.io/herdr-obsidian-vault/configuration.html): settings, keys, public contract, limits
- [Privacy](https://<owner>.github.io/herdr-obsidian-vault/privacy.html): what is read, run, downloaded and written
- [Troubleshooting](https://<owner>.github.io/herdr-obsidian-vault/troubleshooting.html): every message and its fix
- [Check your install](https://<owner>.github.io/herdr-obsidian-vault/verify.html): a checklist on the sample vault and a report template
- [How it works](https://<owner>.github.io/herdr-obsidian-vault/how-it-works.html): files, data flow, caching, rendering
